1.explanation:
• runner-test.js covers how Lighthouse’s runner collects and assigns runtimeSettings (including UA and device) to the LHR.  
• config/default-config-test.js and config/config-test.js define default emulation settings (emulatedFormFactor, screenEmulation, and the UA override) and verify config behavior.  
• gather/driver-test.js tests the driver’s getUserAgent implementation, which is responsible for retrieving the actual UA Chrome/DevTools uses during the run.  
• report/report-generator-test.js ensures those runtimeSettings properties (device, UA, throttling) are correctly injected into the final report object.  
• report/html/renderer/util-test.js covers formatting and rendering of runtimeSettings in the HTML report, which is where the mismatched UA string appears in the UI.  
Together, these files span the path from collecting the UA to displaying it, and are essential for diagnosing why the displayed UA doesn’t match the network logs.
1.bug_scenario: The issue is that Lighthouse’s “Runtime settings” panel shows a single user-agent string (the emulated CrOS/Chrome UA), but the actual page fetches recorded in the webserver’s access.log use a different UA (the Android/Chrome mobile UA) alongside the emulated one. In the first screenshot (Lighthouse Extension 3.0.2) you see “Device: Emulated Nexus 5X” and “User agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; CrOS x86_64 10820.0.0) … Chrome/69.0.3473.0 Safari/537.36” in the report, yet the log below shows two GET /index.html requests, one with a Mobile Safari UA (Chrome/66…) and one with the CrOS UA. In the second screenshot (Chrome DevTools Lighthouse 3.0.0-beta.0) you see the same UA in the UI but only the Android UA in the log, so the UA reported by Lighthouse doesn’t match the one actually used. The feature that gathers, stores, and renders runtime settings (especially the user agent and device emulation) is thus out of sync with the real network‐request UA.
